args.summary: The latest deploy of checkout-api (v2.3.1, prod, seq 3) caused failing health checks in production. In response, the service was rolled back in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback verification: all regions running v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate 0.002. Note: v2.3.1-rc had previously been unhealthy in staging (seq 2) before v2.3.1 was promoted to production.
args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
All done. Here's a summary:

1. **Diagnosed the issue**: checkout-api's latest production deploy, **v2.3.1**, was unhealthy (health checks failing). Notably, its release candidate v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging before promotion.
2. **Rolled back** checkout-api in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to **v2.3.0**, the most recent release that was healthy in production.
3. **Verified recovery**: all regions now running v2.3.0, service is healthy, error rate 0.002.
4. **Opened a SEV2 incident** for checkout-api documenting the failing deploy and the rollback actions; the on-call engineer has been paged.

Recommend following up on why v2.3.1 was promoted to production despite v2.3.1-rc being unhealthy in staging.
